tips.title: Removing Seam Lines on Fuselage Halves with Tamiya Extra Thin
tips.text: After gluing fuselage halves with Tamiya Extra Thin Cement, clamp them and let cure for 30 minutes. Run a bead of liquid cement along the seam inside the fuselage with a fine brush — the melted plastic slightly squeezes out, creating a weld bead. After 24 hours, sand the seam with 400 grit, then 800 grit sanding sticks. If a visible line remains, apply a thin layer of Vallejo Plastic Putty, let dry, and sand again. Finally, restore any lost surface detail (rivets, panel lines) with an RB Productions scriber.

tips.title: Assembling Multi-Part Gun Barrels (Trumpeter, AFV Club)
tips.text: Use a fine-tipped applicator to apply Tamiya Cement in a thin line along the barrel joints. Align the parts precisely with a flat surface, such as a Tamiya Assembly Mat. Clamp with a Tamiya Quick Clamp for 10 minutes. For Trumpeter’s 1/35 barrels, use a small pin vise to insert into the bore to prevent rotation. For AFV Club parts, use a hobby knife to slightly score the inner walls for better adhesion. Allow to cure fully before painting.

tips.title: Using Jigs for Wing Alignment (Arma Hobby, ICM)
tips.text: Create a wing jig from a piece of 1/4" acrylic using a laser cutter for precision. For Arma Hobby’s 1/72 wings, mark the centerline with a Sharpie and position the wing on the jig. Secure with double-sided tape and a small clamp. For ICM’s 1/48 wings, use a thin brass rod as a pivot point to align the leading edge. Check alignment with a digital caliper to ensure 0.005" tolerance. Repeat for both wings.

tips.title: Installing Photo-Etch Parts (Eduard, Clear Prop Models)
tips.text: Use a fine-tipped pin vise to insert Eduard’s photo-etch parts into their slots. For Clear Prop Models’ delicate parts, apply a drop of Tamiya Super Cement on the slot before inserting. Use a magnifying lamp (10x) to align the parts precisely. For complex pieces, apply a small amount of Alclad II Primer to the fit area to prevent warping. Let dry, then paint with Vallejo Model Color for better adhesion.

tips.title: Dry-Fitting Strategies for Assembling Tracks (Meng, Roden)
tips.text: For Meng’s 1/35 tracks, dry-fit all links on a flat surface using a Tamiya Track Aligner. Check for gaps by pressing the links together with a pin vise. For Roden’s vinyl tracks, use a clear acrylic sheet as a base to lay out the track pattern. Ensure each link is spaced 0.025" apart. If using workable tracks, apply a thin coat of Tamiya Plastic Cement to the joints before assembly. For both types, use a 1:1 mix of Tamiya Cement and water to lubricate the links during assembly.
